# `glas.lock` - The Glas Manifest

The glas.lock format is line-based. Each directive starts with a keyword
on a line, followed by values that are parsed specifically by the
directive's handler. 3 directives are considered top-level: `lockfile`,
`klar`, and `package`. Other valid directives are handled under the
`package` directive.

We mainly went for a custom format over Klon for performance (Klon needs
to tokenize and parse an AST before decoding) and to avoid reflection.

See a sample of the lockfile format in [lockfile_sample.txt](./lockfile_sample.txt).

```glaslock
# Generated by Glas. Do not edit.
lockfile v2
klar v0.0.1

package proicons/react v0.0.1 from npm
    for workspace mylang
    dependency react v19.0.0 from npm
    registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
    integrity sha512-abc123
```

Lockfiles are not designed for human editing, but they can still be audited.

## Syntax

- Line comments are defined using `#`.
- Leading and trailing whitespace around lines are insignificant
- The file must start with a `lockfile` directive, followed by `klar`. No other order is allowed.
    - `lockfile`: The version of the lockfile format
    - `klar`: The version of Klar that was used to generate the lockfile
- A package is defined using `package <name> from <source> [git-commit]`. The source must be one of: `git`, `local`, `npm`, or `workspace`. `git-commit` is only accepted when the source is Git.
- Under the `package` directive are subdirectives associated with the package. See `expectedSources` in [parse.go](./parse.go) for the list of supported directives, and the package sources they are compatible with.
- Values colliding with directives are valid
- String quoting and escaping are unsupported

## Tree-sitter

A [Tree-sitter](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter) parser for glas.lock is available in the [klarlanguage/tree-sitter-glaslock](https://github.com/klarlanguage/tree-sitter-glaslock) repository.

## Package Headers

[lockfile.go](./lockfile.go) defines `PackageHeader`, which determines the identity of packages. While packages in the `glas.pack` manifest must have unique names, names of packages in the lockfile don't. Packages may rely on different versions of the same package. To identify the exact version, a package header is used. Package headers can be hashed for storing as map keys.

```go
type PackageHeader struct {
	Name      string // Always the name of the package from the manifest
	Version   version.Version
	From      PackageSource
	GitCommit string // The resolved commit number, if from Git
	Hash      PkgHash
}
```
